channel.title: Nature Communications
channel.description:
Nature Communications is an open access, multidisciplinary journal dedicated to publishing high-quality research in all areas of the biological, health, physical, chemical and Earth sciences. Papers published by the journal aim to represent important advances of significance to specialists within each field.

We are committed to providing an efficient service for both authors and readers. Our team of independent editors make rapid and fair publication decisions. Prompt dissemination of accepted papers to a wide readership and beyond is achieved through a programme of continuous online publication.

item.title: Molecularly engineered zwitterionic‑fluorinated hydrogel electrolyte for durable Ah-level zinc-ion batteries
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 01 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77562-5

Aqueous zinc-ion batteries promise safe energy storage but suffer from dendrites and side reactions. Here, authors engineer a zwitterionic fluorinated hydrogel electrolyte to suppress these issues, enabling durable, dendrite free, Ah-level pouch cells.
item.dc:title: Molecularly engineered zwitterionic‑fluorinated hydrogel electrolyte for durable Ah-level zinc-ion batteries

item.title: Genome mining of the tumor microbiome reveals biosynthetic diversity and potential pathology-modulating metabolites
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 01 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78166-9

Here, Pulliam and colleagues characterize the metabolites encoded by tumor-inhabiting microbes and their potential role in cancer pathology.
item.dc:title: Genome mining of the tumor microbiome reveals biosynthetic diversity and potential pathology-modulating metabolites

item.title: Structural basis of voltage gating in a partially activated K<sup>+</sup> channel
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 01 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78089-5

The process by which the voltage sensor electromechanically couples to the pore in K+ channels is not fully understood. A cryo-EM structure of a partially activated state, together with computational modeling and MD simulations, clarifies the mechanistic basis for electromechanical coupling.
item.dc:title: Structural basis of voltage gating in a partially activated K<sup>+</sup> channel

item.title: Parasitological efficacy of sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine and amodiaquine for seasonal malaria chemoprevention in Africa
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 01 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78189-2

In this study, the authors show that post-treatment desethylamodiaquine concentration is the primary pharmacokinetic determinant of protection against malaria infection in African children who are given sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine and amodiaquine for seasonal malaria chemoprevention, with little apparent effect from sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine.
item.dc:title: Parasitological efficacy of sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine and amodiaquine for seasonal malaria chemoprevention in Africa

item.title: A multiplexed wearable microfluidic platform for non-invasive sweat-inspired monitoring of plant guttation biomarkers
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 01 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77955-6

Plant sensors are emerging as key tools for precision agriculture, yet continuous monitoring of biomarkers in plant biofluids remains underdeveloped. Here, the authors introduce PlantIonics, a wearable microfluidic electrochemical platform for multiplexed, in situ analysis of guttation fluid. The system enables continuous, noninvasive monitoring of stress-associated plant physiological and metabolic responses under changing environmental conditions.
item.dc:title: A multiplexed wearable microfluidic platform for non-invasive sweat-inspired monitoring of plant guttation biomarkers

item.title: Wide-bandgap perovskite with homogeneous crystallization and suppressed halogen segregation for efficient perovskite-organic tandem solar cells
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 01 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78267-5

Inhomogeneous crystallization and phase segregation in wide-bandgap perovskite limit the performance of photovoltaic device. Zhu et al. develop an in situ sequential regulation strategy for crystallization, achieving a power conversion efficiency of 28.20% for perovskite-organic tandem solar cells.
item.dc:title: Wide-bandgap perovskite with homogeneous crystallization and suppressed halogen segregation for efficient perovskite-organic tandem solar cells

item.title: Chromosome-scale assembly of yeast genomes using enzyme-free, dense optical genome mapping
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 01 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78211-7

Optical genome mapping (OGM) provides long-range genomic information but relies on sparse enzymatic labeling that restricts resolution in poorly labeled or structurally complex regions. Here the authors assemble yeast genomes at chromosome scale using dense OGM, resolving large repetitive regions.
item.dc:title: Chromosome-scale assembly of yeast genomes using enzyme-free, dense optical genome mapping

item.title: Cross-border electricity tariffs undermine power system efficiency, decarbonization and reliability in North America
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 01 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77773-w

Analysis of a decade of New York power-market data and simulations shows that tariffs on Canadian electricity imports could raise prices and emissions, diminish economic benefits, and weaken grid reliability during peak demand and extreme weather.
item.dc:title: Cross-border electricity tariffs undermine power system efficiency, decarbonization and reliability in North America
